parsed.attack: The incumbent is Mike Holt Enterprises, which is what instructors and journeymen already recommend for this exam, already sells practice questions with the code tables, and already owns the instructor referral loop this idea needs, built over four decades. Behind it sits NFPA, which publishes the NEC, operates NFPA LiNK as a subscription digital code platform with search and an AI assistant, and holds copyright on the very conduit and box fill tables the product must reproduce, so it can ship recall drills on its own content or simply send a letter. Bolting spaced repetition onto either is a minor release, and the referral channel the idea treats as its loop is already the incumbent's.
parsed.strongest_defence: A 29-dollar single-table micro-tool sits far below the 200 to 500 dollar price floor those businesses need, and their economics rest on continuing-education credit hours, instructor commissions and institutional subscriptions, none of which a one-time consumer purchase feeds; down-market self-serve is a segment they have never served and would cannibalize their own course sales to enter. Their products are reference and course material, not a daily recall habit in the eight weeks before a booked date.
parsed.verdict_reason: The incumbent's price floor genuinely protects the niche, but it already owns the instructor channel the loop depends on and the copyright on the content, so the wedge is cheap for it to take whenever it wants.
